rendered: Energy density: the review says LIBs have risen since their commercial debut in 1991[1], stating that they increased from 150 to 250 Wh kg^− 1[2]. That is a rise by a factor of about 1.7[3] (from the review's own stated values). Battery cost: the review says it has steadily decreased from over $1000 kWh^− 1 in 2008[4] to around $130 kWh^− 1 in 2020[5]. That is a fall by a factor of about 7.7[6] (computed from the stated endpoints; the starting value is given only as over $1000). The review's introduction also gives a DOE-backed cost reduction of reduce LIB cost by nearly eightfold[7]. Caveat: the factors cover different periods, since the energy density starting point is the commercial debut in 1991[8] and the cost starting point is 2008[9].
